claims.source: We treated the CAGGCre-ER/Kdm1afl/fl MEFs with a KDM1A inhibitor, CBB3001, that we previously developed (Guo et al., 2022; Hoang et al., 2018) and found that the protein level of EZH2 is significantly decreased by CBB3001 (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Kdm1a silencing caused the downregulation of EZH2 protein and the Kdm1a silencing-induced EZH2 reduction is reversed by the treatment of 26 S proteasome inhibitor, MG132.
claims.source: We found that Kdm1a silencing caused the downregulation of EZH2 protein and the Kdm1a silencing-induced EZH2 reduction is reversed by the treatment of 26 S proteasome inhibitor, MG132, added in the last 6 hr of the experiment (Figure 1G; Guo et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: Expression of the wild-type, but not the catalytically dead mutant, can suppress the si-Kdm1a-3'UTR effects of the endogenous Kdm1a on EZH2 proteins.
claims.source: We found that while the siRNA against the 3'UTR region (si-Kdm1a-3'UTR) of the endogenous Kdm1a leads to the downregulation of EZH2 in the absence of the Flag-KDM1A, expression of the wild-type, but not the catalytically dead mutant, can suppress the si-Kdm1a-3'UTR effects of the endogenous Kdm1a on EZH2 proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C.

claims.claim: KDM1A is required to maintain the protein stability of EZH2 to prevent the disassembly of PRC2.
claims.source: Our studies indicate that KDM1A is required to maintain the protein stability of EZH2 to prevent the disassembly of PRC2.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claims.claim: The levels of EZH2 and SUZ12 proteins are significantly increased in the mouse L3mbtl3 null embryos, as compared to that of the wild-type littermates.
claims.source: We repeatedly found that the levels of EZH2 and SUZ12 proteins are significantly increased in the mouse L3mbtl3 null embryos, which died at E17.5–19.5, as compared to that of the wild-type littermates (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: The loss of L3mbtl3 caused the accumulation of EZH2 protein and the increased level of trimethylated H3K27 in mouse embryonic fibroblasts.
claims.source: In mouse embryonic fibroblasts isolated from the wild-type or L3mbtl3 homozygous deletion mutant embryos, the loss of L3mbtl3 caused the accumulation of EZH2 protein and the increased level of trimethylated H3K27 (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Homozygous loss of L3mbtl3 in the brain of the L3mbtl3fl/fl/Nestin-Cre mice accumulated EZH2 and SUZ12 proteins, as compared with that of L3mbtl3fl/+/Nestin-Cre mice.
claims.source: We found that homozygous loss of L3mbtl3 in the brain of the L3mbtl3fl/fl/Nestin-Cre mice survived, but the brain extracts accumulated EZH2 and SUZ12 proteins, as compared with that of L3mbtl3fl/+/Nestin-Cre mice (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: The protein levels of EZH2 and trimethylated H3K27 accumulate in the L3mbtl3 conditional null mutant brains, as compared to that of the control wild-type littermates.
claims.source: Our immunostaining of the brain sections from the wild-type and L3mbtl3fl/fl/Nestin-Cre null mutant animals also revealed that the protein levels of EZH2 and trimethylated H3K27 accumulate in the L3mbtl3 conditional null mutant brains, as compared to that of the control wild-type littermates (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: The induced co-deletion of Kdm1a and L3mbtl3 in the CAGGCre-ER/ Kdm1afl/fl/L3mbtl3fl/fl MEFs leads to the restoration of the EZH2 and H3K27me3 protein levels in the MEFs.
claims.source: However, the induced co-deletion of Kdm1a and L3mbtl3 in the CAGGCre-ER/ Kdm1afl/fl/L3mbtl3fl/fl MEFs leads to the restoration of the EZH2 and H3K27me3 protein levels in the MEFs.
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section.

claims.claim: While Kdm1a silencing reduced EZH2 protein levels, co-silencing of L3mbtl3 and Kdm1a stabilized EZH2 protein levels in Kdm1a-deficient cells.
claims.source: Our study revealed that while Kdm1a silencing reduced EZH2 protein levels, co-silencing of L3mbtl3 and Kdm1a stabilized EZH2 protein levels in Kdm1a-deficient cells (Figure 2F and G).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2F and G.

claims.claim: EZH2 protein levels are elevated in the CRISPR-Cas9-mediated L3mbtl3 knockout (KO) cells than the parental wild-type HCT116 cells.
claims.source: Analysis of EZH2 protein revealed that EZH2 protein levels are elevated in the CRISPR-Cas9-mediated L3mbtl3 knockout (KO) cells than the parental wild-type HCT116 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: L3MBTL3 overexpression in HCT116 cells caused the downregulation of EZH2 protein.
claims.source: Our studies showed that L3MBTL3 overexpression in HCT116 cells caused the downregulation of EZH2 protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: The protein level of EZH2 is tightly regulated by L3MBTL3.
claims.source: Collectively, these studies indicate the protein level of EZH2 is tightly regulated by L3MBTL3.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claims.claim: L3MBTL3 recruits the CRL4DCAF5 ubiquitin E3 ligase complex to target substrates, such as DNMT1, SOX2, and SMARCC1, for ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis.
claims.source: Our previous studies have shown that L3MBTL3 recruits the CRL4DCAF5 ubiquitin E3 ligase complex to target substrates, such as DNMT1, SOX2, and SMARCC1, for ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis (Guo et al., 2022; Leng et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature from the authors' group.

claims.claim: Homozygous mutation of the Dcaf5 alleles caused significant elevation of EZH2 and H3K27me3 protein levels.
claims.source: We found that homozygous mutation of the Dcaf5 alleles also caused significant elevation of EZH2 and H3K27me3 protein levels (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Loss of Dcaf5 leads to increased levels of EZH2 and H3K27me3 staining, as compared with that of control wild-type littermates.
claims.source: Immunostaining of the embryonic brain sections revealed that loss of Dcaf5 leads to increased levels of EZH2 and H3K27me3 staining, as compared with that of control wild-type littermates (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: siRNA-mediated co-silencing of Dcaf5 and Kdm1a in H1299 cells stabilized EZH2 protein in Kdm1a-deficient cells.
claims.source: Consistent with these animal studies, siRNA-mediated co-silencing of Dcaf5 and Kdm1a in H1299 cells with two representative siRNAs stabilized EZH2 protein in Kdm1a-deficient cells (Figure 3E and F).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3E and F.

claims.claim: The CRL4DCAF5 ubiquitin ligase complex is involved in the proteolytic degradation of EZH2 to regulate the H3K27me3 levels during mouse development and in cultured cancer cells.
claims.source: These results indicate that the CRL4DCAF5 ubiquitin ligase complex is involved in the proteolytic degradation of EZH2 to regulate the H3K27me3 levels during mouse development and in cultured cancer cells.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claims.claim: EZH2 contains a conserved lysine residue, Lys20 (K20), in the putative SET7 methylation consensus motif (R/K-S/T/V-K) that is very similar to that of the Lys42 (K42) methylation degron motif in SOX2.
claims.source: To further investigate EZH2 regulation, we examined and found that EZH2 contains a conserved lysine residue, Lys20 (K20), in the putative SET7 methylation consensus motif (R/K-S/T/V-K) that is very similar to that of the Lys42 (K42) methylation degron motif in SOX2 (Figure 4A; Zhang et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: The recombinant GST-KDM1A protein can effectively remove the methyl group of the monomethylated K20 peptide.
claims.source: We mixed and incubated the monomethylated K20 peptide with purified GST-KDM1A and found that the recombinant GST-KDM1A protein can effectively remove the methyl group of the monomethylated K20 peptide (Figure 4C), indicating that the monomethylated K20 in EZH2 serves as a direct substrate of KDM1A.
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: The monomethylated K20 in EZH2 serves as a direct substrate of KDM1A.
claims.source: We mixed and incubated the monomethylated K20 peptide with purified GST-KDM1A and found that the recombinant GST-KDM1A protein can effectively remove the methyl group of the monomethylated K20 peptide (Figure 4C), indicating that the monomethylated K20 in EZH2 serves as a direct substrate of KDM1A.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section based on experimental data.

claims.claim: Loss of KDM1A destabilizes both EZH2 and EZH2-K20me and reduces the level of H3K27me3 in HCT116 cells, but treatment of KDM1A-deficient cells with the protease inhibitor MG132 restored the levels of EZH2, EZH2-K20me, and H3K27me3.
claims.source: Loss of KDM1A destabilizes both EZH2 and EZH2-K20me and reduces the level of H3K27me3 in HCT116 cells, but treatment of KDM1A-deficient cells with the protease inhibitor MG132 restored the levels of EZH2, EZH2-K20me, and H3K27me3 (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Nestin-Cre-mediated loss of Kdm1a in the mouse caused the reduction of both the K20 methylation level of EZH2 and the EZH2 protein levels, as well as the downregulation of trimethylated H3K27 levels.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4E, Nestin-Cre-mediated loss of Kdm1a in the mouse caused the reduction of both the K20 methylation level of EZH2 and the EZH2 protein levels, as well as the downregulation of trimethylated H3K27 levels.
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Homozygous loss of L3mbtl3 resulted in an increased level of EZH2 K20me.
claims.source: Conversely, homozygous loss of L3mbtl3 resulted in an increased level of EZH2 K20me (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: Transient overexpression of SET7 resulted in a reduction of EZH2 protein and H3K27 trimethylation levels in HCT116 cells.
claims.source: We found that transient overexpression of SET7 resulted in a reduction of EZH2 protein and H3K27 trimethylation levels in HCT116 cells (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4G.

claims.claim: The K20-methylated EZH2 fraction is enriched in the L3MBTL3 co-immunoprecipitation with EZH2 in SET7-expressed and MG132-treated cells.
claims.source: In addition, the K20-methylated EZH2 fraction is enriched in the L3MBTL3 co-immunoprecipitation with EZH2 in SET7-expressed and MG132-treated cells (Figure 4H).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4H.

claims.claim: While silencing of Kdm1a reduced the protein level of ectopically and stably expressed Flag-tagged EZH2 in H1299 cells, co-silencing of Set7 with Kdm1a siRNAs effectively re-stabilized Flag-EZH2 protein in KDM1A-deficient cells.
claims.source: Our investigation further showed that while silencing of Kdm1a reduced the protein level of ectopically and stably expressed Flag-tagged EZH2 in H1299 cells, co-silencing of Set7 with Kdm1a siRNAs effectively re-stabilized Flag-EZH2 protein in KDM1A-deficient cells (Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: SET7 is capable of methylating K20 in EZH2, and that the methylated K20 of EZH2 is targeted by L3MBTL3 for methylation-dependent proteolysis of EZH2.
claims.source: These studies indicate that SET7 is capable of methylating K20 in EZH2, and that the methylated K20 of EZH2 is targeted by L3MBTL3 for methylation-dependent proteolysis of EZH2.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claims.claim: Silencing of Phf20l1 by two independent siRNAs both induced the degradation of EZH2 protein, and co-silencing of Phf20l1 and L3mbtl3 restored EZH2 protein levels.
claims.source: We found that silencing of Phf20l1 by two independent siRNAs both induced the degradation of EZH2 protein, and co-silencing of Phf20l1 and L3mbtl3 restored EZH2 protein levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and C).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and C.

claims.claim: PHF20L1 normally prevents the proteolysis of EZH2 by the methylation-dependent proteolysis.
claims.source: These studies indicate that PHF20L1 normally prevents the proteolysis of EZH2 by the methylation-dependent proteolysis.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claims.claim: Ectopic expression of SET7 led to substantially increased K20 methylation of EZH2 and H3K27me3 proteins in T47D cells.
claims.source: We found that ectopic expression of SET7 led to substantially increased K20 methylation of EZH2 and H3K27me3 proteins (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claims.claim: SET7 expression and increased K20 methylation of EZH2 in T47D cells led to a substantial reduction of the phosphorylated serine 21 (S21) in EZH2.
claims.source: However, while SET7 expression reduced EZH2 protein in HCT116 cells (Figure 4G), expression of SET7 in T47D cells did not cause significant downregulation of EZH2 protein, although the levels of K20 methylation is increased after SET7 is expressed (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D). On the other hand, SET7 expression and increased K20 methylation of EZH2 in T47D cells led to a substantial reduction of the phosphorylated serine 21 (S21) in EZH2, a site previously reported to be phosphorylated by the active AKT activity (Cha et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claims.claim: The methylation of K20 may negatively regulate the phosphorylation of S21 of EZH2.
claims.source: Our results from T47D cells indicate that transient expression of SET7 catalyzes an increased level of the mono-methylation of K20 and also causes the decrease of the phosphorylation of S21 in EZH2 in T47D cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D), suggesting that the methylation of K20 may negatively regulate the phosphorylation of S21 of EZH2.
claims.evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on experimental data.

claims.claim: The methylated K20 levels of EZH2 gradually increased during mouse embryogenesis from E14.5, E18.5, to the first postnatal day after birth (P0), associated with the gradual downregulation of EZH2 protein and H3K27 trimethylation levels at these development stages.
claims.source: Our studies revealed that the methylated K20 levels of EZH2 gradually increased during mouse embryogenesis from E14.5, E18.5, to the first postnatal day after birth (P0), associated with the gradual downregulation of EZH2 protein and H3K27 trimethylation levels at these development stages (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: The downregulation of the trimethylated H3K27 is accompanied by the increased levels of S21-phosphorylated form of EZH2 during the indicated developmental stages.
claims.source: The downregulation of the trimethylated H3K27 is also accompanied by the increased levels of S21-phosphorylated form of EZH2 during the indicated developmental stages, suggesting that the activity of EZH2 is reduced by both K20-methylation-dependent proteolysis and S21-phosphorylation dependent activity inhibition (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: The activity of EZH2 is reduced by both K20-methylation-dependent proteolysis and S21-phosphorylation dependent activity inhibition.
claims.source: The downregulation of the trimethylated H3K27 is also accompanied by the increased levels of S21-phosphorylated form of EZH2 during the indicated developmental stages, suggesting that the activity of EZH2 is reduced by both K20-methylation-dependent proteolysis and S21-phosphorylation dependent activity inhibition (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on experimental data.

claims.claim: L3mbtl3-LacZ is expressed around E12-E15 during mouse development, with the highly elevated expression of L3MBTL3 around embryonic day E15.
claims.source: The staining of L3mbtl3-LacZ in the developing mouse embryos revealed that L3mbtl3-LacZ is expressed around E12-E15 during mouse development (Figure 5B), with the highly elevated expression of L3MBTL3 around embryonic day E15.
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: L3MBTL3 is expressed during the mouse embryonic stages when the protein levels of EZH2 and H3K27me3 start to decline.
claims.source: These studies suggest that L3MBTL3 is expressed during the mouse embryonic stages when the protein levels of EZH2 and H3K27me3 start to decline.
claims.evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on experimental data.

claims.claim: L3MBTL3 and EZH2 interact in mouse embryonic extracts.
claims.source: In mouse embryonic extracts, our co-immunoprecipitation analysis revealed that L3MBTL3 and EZH2 interact (Figure 5C);
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: The transient expression of wild-type SET7 in 293T cells promoted the interaction between L3MBTL3 and EZH2, but not an inactive SET7 mutant in which the critical histidine 297 is converted to alanine (H297A).
claims.source: and the transient expression of wild-type SET7 in 293T cells promoted the interaction between L3MBTL3 and EZH2, but not an inactive SET7 mutant in which the critical histidine 297 is converted to alanine (H297A, Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: The SET7-promoted binding of EZH2 to L3MBTL3 is dependent on the presence of K20 in EZH2, as the conversion of K20 to arginine (K20R) in EZH2 (EZH2K20R) abolished the EZH2-L3MBTL3 interaction.
claims.source: In addition, the SET7-promoted binding of EZH2 to L3MBTL3 is dependent on the presence of K20 in EZH2, as the conversion of K20 to arginine (K20R) in EZH2 (EZH2K20R) abolished the EZH2-L3MBTL3 interaction (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: While the wild-type EZH2 is reduced by Kdm1a silencing, the EZH2K20R mutant is resistant to the loss of KDM1A.
claims.source: We also found that while the wild-type EZH2 is reduced by Kdm1a silencing, the EZH2K20R mutant is resistant to the loss of KDM1A (Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: The S21A mutation of EZH2 (EZH2S21A) that converts S21 to alanine remains sensitive to Kdm1a silencing, indicating that K20 is still methylated in the EZH2S21A mutant protein.
claims.source: The S21A mutation of EZH2 (EZH2S21A) that converts S21 to alanine remains sensitive to Kdm1a silencing, indicating that K20 is still methylated in the EZH2S21A mutant protein (Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: Co-expression of SET7, L3MBTL3, and DCAF5 are sufficient to promote EZH2 polyubiquitination.
claims.source: Furthermore, co-expression of SET7, L3MBTL3, and DCAF5 are sufficient to promote EZH2 polyubiquitination (Figure 5G), but the EZH2K20R mutant under the same conditions failed to be polyubiquitinated (Figure 5H).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5G.

claims.claim: The EZH2K20R mutant under the same conditions failed to be polyubiquitinated.
claims.source: Furthermore, co-expression of SET7, L3MBTL3, and DCAF5 are sufficient to promote EZH2 polyubiquitination (Figure 5G), but the EZH2K20R mutant under the same conditions failed to be polyubiquitinated (Figure 5H).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5H.

claims.claim: K20 of EZH2 is methylated by SET7, and that L3MBTL3 and CRL4DCAF5 recognize and target the K20-methylated EZH2 protein for ubiquitination-dependent proteolysis.
claims.source: These studies collectively indicate that K20 of EZH2 is methylated by SET7, and that L3MBTL3 and CRL4DCAF5 recognize and target the K20-methylated EZH2 protein for ubiquitination-dependent proteolysis.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claims.claim: The half-lives of EZH2 proteins were reduced after Kdm1a silencing in cells expressing the wild-type and S21A mutant EZH2, but the K20R mutant EZH2 was quite resistant to Kdm1a silencing.
claims.source: We found that the half-lives of EZH2 proteins were reduced after Kdm1a silencing in cells expressing the wild-type and S21A mutant EZH2, but the K20R mutant EZH2 was quite resistant to Kdm1a silencing (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Treatment of T47D cells with MK2206, an AKT inhibitor, inhibited AKT-mediated S21 phosphorylation of EZH2 and increased levels of H3K27me3 due to the reactivation of EZH2 methyltransferase activity as S21-phosphorylation inhibits EZH2 activity, but the total EZH2 protein levels were not significantly altered.
claims.source: Indeed, we found that treatment of T47D cells with MK2206, an AKT inhibitor, inhibited AKT-mediated S21 phosphorylation of EZH2 and increased levels of H3K27me3 due to the reactivation of EZH2 methyltransferase activity as S21-phosphorylation inhibits EZH2 activity, but the total EZH2 protein levels were not significantly altered (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 2B), consistent with the original report (Cha et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: MK2206 reduced the levels of EZH2 protein, associated with the decreased levels of the phosphorylated AKT, reduced phosphorylated S21 in EZH2, diminished levels of H3K27me3, concurrent with increased levels of the K20 methylated EZH2 protein in MEFs.
claims.source: We repeatedly found that MK2206 reduced the levels of EZH2 protein, associated with the decreased levels of the phosphorylated AKT, reduced phosphorylated S21 in EZH2, diminished levels of H3K27me3, concurrent with increased levels of the K20 methylated EZH2 protein in MEFs (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: There is an inverse relationship between the levels of K20-methylation and S21-phosphorylation of EZH2, and that increased levels of K20 methylation after AKT inhibition promote the proteolysis of EZH2 in primary MEFs.
claims.source: Our studies in the primary MEFs suggest that in contrast to the response of T47D cells (Figure 6A), these is an inverse relationship between the levels of K20-methylation and S21-phosphorylation of EZH2, and that increased levels of K20 methylation after AKT inhibition promote the proteolysis of EZH2 (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claims.claim: Increasing concentrations of MK2206 caused the downregulation of EZH2 protein, reduced the levels of phosphorylated AKT and phosphorylated S21, and consequently decreased the levels of H3K27me3 in PA-1 cells.
claims.source: We next treated human teratocarcinoma PA-1 cells with various doses of MK2206 and found that increasing concentrations of MK2206 also caused the downregulation of EZH2 protein, reduced the levels of phosphorylated AKT and phosphorylated S21, and consequently decreased the levels of H3K27me3 (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: The downregulation of AKT-mediated processes are associated with the increased levels of K20 methylation in EZH2 in PA-1 cells.
claims.source: The downregulation of AKT-mediated processes are associated with the increased levels of K20 methylation in EZH2 (Figure 6C), similar to the response of MEFs to MK2206 (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: Reduction of S21 phosphorylation in MEFs facilitates the methylation of K20 in EZH2 by SET7, leading to EZH2 proteolysis and consequently reducing the trimethylated H3K27 levels.
claims.source: The results in MEFs, PA-1, and H1299 cells all showed that reduction of S21 phosphorylation in MEFs facilitates the methylation of K20 in EZH2 by SET7, leading to EZH2 proteolysis and consequently reducing the trimethylated H3K27 levels.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claims.claim: EZH2 is regulated by a methylation-phosphorylation switch of EZH2 in MEFs, PA-1, and H1299 cells.
claims.source: These studies indicate that EZH2 is regulated by a methylation-phosphorylation switch of EZH2 in MEFs, PA-1, and H1299 cells.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claims.claim: Ectopic and stable expression of HA-tagged L3MBTL3 in T47D cells conferred the EZH2 proteolytic response to MK2206.
claims.source: We found that ectopic and stable expression of HA-tagged L3MBTL3 in T47D cells conferred the EZH2 proteolytic response to MK2206 (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: Inhibition of AKT leads to the reduced level of EZH2 protein and consequent downregulation of H3K27me3 levels in T47D cells that ectopically express L3MBTL3.
claims.source: Our analysis revealed that inhibition of AKT leads to the reduced level of EZH2 protein and consequent downregulation of H3K27me3 levels in T47D cells that ectopically express L3MBTL3, similar to that of MEFs, PA-1, and H1299 cells (Figure 6B–D, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6B–D, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2C.

claims.claim: EZH2 protein levels in T47D cells did not significantly respond to AKT inhibition is likely caused by the weak L3MBTL3-dependent proteolysis activity of EZH2 in this cell line.
claims.source: We reasoned that EZH2 protein levels in T47D cells did not significantly respond to AKT inhibition is likely caused by the weak L3MBTL3-dependent proteolysis activity of EZH2 in this cell line, and we tried to further investigate this possibility by using the L3mbtl3 null MEFs that are deficient in targeting the K20-methylation-dependent proteolysis of EZH2 (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: Stated as reasoning in the results section.

claims.claim: MK2206 treatment caused increased levels of H3K27me3 in the L3mbtl3 null MEFs due to the removal of S21 phosphorylation-mediated inhibition on EZH2 and PRC2, whereas AKT inhibition did not cause any further changes in EZH2 protein levels because of L3mbtl3 deletion.
claims.source: Our studies revealed that MK2206 treatment caused increased levels of H3K27me3 in the L3mbtl3 null MEFs due to the removal of S21 phosphorylation-mediated inhibition on EZH2 and PRC2, whereas AKT inhibition did not cause any further changes in EZH2 protein levels because of L3mbtl3 deletion, a result similar to the response of T47D cells to MK2206 (Figure 6A and E).
claims.evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6A and E.

claims.claim: T47D cells may have reduced activities in L3MBTL3 and CRL4DCAF5 ubiquitin E3 ligase activities to target the K20-methylated EZH2 for proteolysis.
claims.source: These studies are consistent with our hypothesis that T47D cells may have reduced activities in L3MBTL3 and CRL4DCAF5 ubiquitin E3 ligase activities to target the K20-methylated EZH2 for proteolysis.
claims.evidence: Stated as a hypothesis in the results section.

claims.claim: AKT inhibition by MK2206 reduced EZH2 protein stability in several cancer cells.
claims.source: Our results are also consistent with other reports showing that AKT inhibition by MK2206 reduced EZH2 protein stability in several cancer cells (Riquelme et al., 2016), indicating the methylation-phosphorylation switch of EZH2 exists in many cells, but T47D is defective in this pathway.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claims.claim: The methylation-phosphorylation switch of EZH2 exists in many cells, but T47D is defective in this pathway.
claims.source: Our results are also consistent with other reports showing that AKT inhibition by MK2206 reduced EZH2 protein stability in several cancer cells (Riquelme et al., 2016), indicating the methylation-phosphorylation switch of EZH2 exists in many cells, but T47D is defective in this pathway.
claims.evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claims.claim: L3mbtl3 is mutated in medulloblastoma and is further implicated in other pathological disorders such as multiple sclerosis, insulin resistance, prostate cancer, and breast cancer.
claims.source: L3mbtl3 is mutated in medulloblastoma and is further implicated in other pathological disorders such as multiple sclerosis, insulin resistance, prostate cancer, and breast cancer (Andlauer et al., 2016; Bonasio et al., 2010; Kar et al., 2016; Lotta et al., 2017; Northcott et al., 2009).

results.result: Loss of Kdm1a in mice causes a dramatic reduction of PRC2 proteins (EZH2, SUZ12, EED) through post-transcriptional mechanisms. This reduction is reversed by proteasome inhibition and requires KDM1A catalytic activity, indicating that KDM1A maintains EZH2 protein stability to prevent PRC2 disassembly.
results.evaluation: Multiple independent experimental approaches (conditional knockout mice, MEFs, chemical inhibition, siRNA knockdown, rescue experiments) consistently demonstrate that loss of KDM1A leads to PRC2 protein reduction (C38-C45). The post-transcriptional mechanism is established by showing unchanged mRNA levels (C41), and proteasome involvement is confirmed by MG132 rescue (C44). The requirement for catalytic activity is demonstrated by rescue experiments (C45).

results.result: Loss of L3mbtl3 or Dcaf5 in mice results in PRC2 accumulation and increased H3K27 trimethylation. L3MBTL3 tightly regulates EZH2 protein levels, and co-deletion of Kdm1a and L3mbtl3 restores EZH2 levels in Kdm1a-deficient cells.
results.evaluation: Multiple genetic models (null embryos, conditional knockouts, CRISPR knockout cells, overexpression) consistently show that loss of L3mbtl3 or Dcaf5 increases EZH2 and H3K27me3 levels (C47-C54, C57-C58). The genetic epistasis experiment showing restoration of EZH2 in double knockouts (C51-C52) provides strong evidence for L3MBTL3 acting downstream of KDM1A in EZH2 regulation.

results.result: EZH2 is methylated at lysine 20 (K20) by SET7, and this methylation promotes EZH2 proteolysis through L3MBTL3 and CRL4DCAF5. KDM1A demethylates K20 to stabilize EZH2.
results.evaluation: The K20 methylation is demonstrated through multiple approaches: in vitro demethylation assays (C62), specific antibody detection in cells and mice (C64-C66), SET7 overexpression effects (C67), and enrichment in L3MBTL3 co-IP (C68). The functional consequences are shown by proteasome inhibitor rescue (C64) and genetic manipulations (C65-C66, C69). The mechanistic link between methylation and proteolysis is well-established.

results.result: K20 methylation is inhibited by AKT-mediated phosphorylation of serine 21 (S21) in EZH2, establishing a methylation-phosphorylation switch. AKT inhibition increases K20 methylation and promotes EZH2 proteolysis in most cell types, while S21 phosphorylation stabilizes EZH2.
results.evaluation: The inverse relationship between K20 methylation and S21 phosphorylation is demonstrated in multiple contexts: SET7 overexpression reduces S21 phosphorylation (C74), developmental time course shows inverse correlation (C76-C77), and AKT inhibition increases K20 methylation while promoting EZH2 degradation in MEFs, PA-1, and H1299 cells (C91-C94). The cell-type specificity (T47D exception) is explained by differential L3MBTL3 expression (C97-C101), strengthening the mechanistic model.

results.result: Ezh2K20R/K20R mutant mice are viable but develop hepatosplenomegaly and show expansion of hematopoietic stem cells and downstream populations in bone marrow, with increased expression of HSC regulators (Runx1, Gata2, Etv6, cFos, Ikaros, Gfi1) and altered expression of EZH2-repressed genes.
results.evaluation: The phenotypic characterization is comprehensive, including organ measurements (C109), flow cytometry quantification of multiple hematopoietic populations (C110-C113), and gene expression analysis (C115-C116). The viability with normal Mendelian ratios (C108) indicates the mutation is not embryonic lethal. The consistency between increased EZH2 protein stability (expected from K20R mutation) and hematopoietic expansion provides mechanistic coherence.

results.result: Ezh2K20R/K20R mutant mice show increased GFI1B expression in spleen, mild-to-moderate reactive hyperplasia, increased EZH2 and H3K27me3 protein levels, and increased proliferating cells. The K20R mutation modulates EZH2 protein stability and induces these pathological changes.
results.evaluation: The splenic phenotype is well-documented through multiple approaches: RT-PCR showing increased Gfi1b mRNA (C125), immunohistochemistry and Western blotting confirming increased GFI1B protein (C127-C128), histological analysis showing hyperplasia (C120), and Ki67 staining indicating increased proliferation (C123). The increased EZH2 and H3K27me3 levels (C122) are consistent with the stabilizing effect of the K20R mutation.

results.result: EZH2 is regulated by a methylation-phosphorylation switch where K20 methylation-dependent proteolysis is negatively controlled by AKT-mediated S21 phosphorylation. This switch regulates PRC2 activity and hematopoiesis through dynamic control of EZH2 stability and enzymatic activity.
results.evaluation: This integrative model is supported by the convergence of multiple lines of evidence: the opposing effects of K20 methylation (proteolysis) and S21 phosphorylation (activity inhibition) on EZH2 (C137), the mutual exclusivity of these modifications (C141-C142), the developmental regulation showing coordinated changes (C76-C78), and the in vivo consequences in Ezh2K20R mice (C8-C9). The model coherently explains all major experimental observations.

results.result: The CRL4DCAF5 ubiquitin ligase complex, recruited by L3MBTL3, is involved in proteolytic degradation of EZH2 to regulate H3K27me3 levels during mouse development and in cultured cancer cells.
results.evaluation: The role of DCAF5 is demonstrated through multiple approaches: CRISPR-generated Dcaf5 knockout mice show elevated EZH2 and H3K27me3 (C57-C58), and siRNA-mediated co-silencing experiments in cells confirm the epistatic relationship (C59). The consistency with prior work on L3MBTL3-CRL4DCAF5 targeting other substrates (C56) provides mechanistic coherence.

results.result: PHF20L1 prevents the proteolysis of EZH2 by protecting the K20-methylated form. Loss of PHF20L1 destabilizes EZH2 protein, and this effect is rescued by co-silencing L3mbtl3.
results.evaluation: The protective role of PHF20L1 is demonstrated by siRNA experiments showing that PHF20L1 loss induces EZH2 degradation (C71), which is rescued by co-silencing L3mbtl3 (C71). This establishes PHF20L1 as a reader protein that protects methylated EZH2 from L3MBTL3-mediated degradation, analogous to its role with SOX2.

results.result: L3MBTL3 is expressed during mouse embryonic development (E12-E15) when EZH2 levels decline. L3MBTL3 interacts with EZH2 in a SET7- and K20-dependent manner, and SET7, L3MBTL3, and DCAF5 are sufficient to promote K20-dependent EZH2 polyubiquitination.
results.evaluation: The temporal expression of L3MBTL3 during development is shown by LacZ reporter staining (C79), correlating with EZH2 decline (C80). The molecular interactions are demonstrated by co-IP experiments showing SET7-dependent (C82) and K20-dependent (C83) binding. The sufficiency for ubiquitination is shown by reconstitution experiments (C86), with K20R mutation abolishing this effect (C87). The resistance of K20R and S21A mutants to KDM1A loss (C84-C85) provides additional functional validation.

results.result: The methylation-phosphorylation switch operates differentially in various cell types. T47D cells show defective EZH2 proteolytic response to AKT inhibition due to low L3MBTL3 expression, which can be restored by ectopic L3MBTL3 expression. L3mbtl3 null MEFs phenocopy T47D cells in their response to AKT inhibition.
results.evaluation: The cell-type specificity is rigorously demonstrated: T47D cells lack EZH2 proteolytic response to MK2206 (C90), which is explained by low L3MBTL3 expression (C105) and restored by ectopic L3MBTL3 (C97-C98). The L3mbtl3 null MEFs show the same response pattern as T47D cells (C100), providing genetic validation of the hypothesis (C99, C101). This explains apparent discrepancies with prior literature (C102-C103).

results.result: PRC2 plays essential roles in embryonic development, cell fate determination, and various developmental processes. EZH2 is frequently altered in cancers and serves as a therapeutic target. S21 phosphorylation by AKT inhibits EZH2 activity and facilitates tumorigenesis, but the physiological role of S21-phosphorylated EZH2 remains unclear.
results.evaluation: These are well-established background claims supported by appropriate citations to prior literature (C11-C25). The knowledge gap regarding S21 phosphorylation (C26) provides context for the current study. These claims accurately represent the state of the field.

results.result: Protein lysine methylation regulates chromatin structure and gene expression through histone modifications. Many non-histone proteins are methylated by SET7 and demethylated by KDM1A, leading to methylation-dependent proteolysis. Loss of Kdm1a causes embryonic lethality and impairs stem cell function, but the molecular targets remain unclear.
results.evaluation: These background claims are well-supported by citations to prior literature, including the authors' own work (C27-C36). The knowledge gap regarding KDM1A targets (C37) provides rationale for the current study. These claims accurately represent established knowledge and set up the study's objectives.

results.result: In T47D cells, SET7 expression increases K20 methylation without causing significant EZH2 degradation. The fraction of EZH2 not modified by K20 methylation or S21 phosphorylation is likely the active form for H3K27 trimethylation. The PHF20L1-protected, K20-methylated EZH2 fraction may also be catalytically active.
results.evaluation: While the observation in T47D cells is documented (C73), the claims about which EZH2 fractions are catalytically active (C138, C140) are speculative and not directly tested. The manuscript acknowledges these as possibilities requiring further investigation. The T47D observation is explained by low L3MBTL3 levels, but the activity states of different EZH2 modifications remain to be determined experimentally.

results.result: L3mbtl3 is mutated in various cancers and pathological disorders. EZH2 alterations are frequently associated with cancers, and lysine methylation-dependent proteolysis may be affected in cancer cells. GFI1B is a proto-oncogenic transcriptional regulator that interacts with EZH2 and GATA1.
results.evaluation: These claims are supported by appropriate citations to prior literature (C104, C106, C118-C119, C126, C129-C130). The speculation about altered proteolysis in cancer (C107) is reasonable given the documented L3MBTL3 mutations and differential expression, though it requires further investigation. These claims provide important context for understanding the pathological implications of the findings.

results.result: AKT inhibition by MK2206 reduced EZH2 protein stability in several cancer cells, as reported in prior literature.
results.evaluation: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature (Riquelme et al., 2016) and is consistent with the authors' findings in most cell types. It helps explain the cell-type specificity observed and validates the methylation-phosphorylation switch model.
